text:
maria: Heads up — planning June 28 webinar + benchmark blog. Need a refreshed battlecard vs cloud AI platforms, LLM APIs, and infra vendors. Quick sync on core claims + inbound routing?
aj: +1. I think we should structure claims into three buckets: performance/latency, cost economics, and reliability/operational controls. Short, deployable soundbites for SDRs.
leo: For performance soundbite: 'Predictable inference at scale' with a bench callout — show tail-latency improvement on streaming convo workloads (2k tokens). Need to define bench config.
sanya: Agree. Tactically: avoid naming competitors in outward-facing slides, but the battlecard should map competitor weaknesses -> our counters. Example: clouds = noisy latency, LLM APIs = limited rollouts/versioning, infra vendors = ops burden.
derek: Bench proposal (short):
```
1) 2k-token streaming convo — measure p95/p99 tail
2) Short completions — cost per 1k tokens vs throughput
3) Bulk embeddings — throughput and unit cost
Model mix: open model X (quantized) + a Redwood-verified baseline
Hardware: mixed GPU pool to show routing fallbacks
```
Link to draft bench doc: https://docs.google.com/example
maria: Add a customer vignette — fintech using Redwood Private to meet compliance + keep latency SLOs. That sells both Private + Dedicated as a progression.
aj: Inbound routing idea: tag incoming leads by use-case (latency-sensitive, regulated, cost-conscious). SDRs get templated playbooks per tag. Also add a quick flowchart (hosted -> dedicated -> private) to show predictable escalation.
leo: Webinar format idea: eng runtime lead (bench) + customer panel + solutions demo. Slides: 10m bench findings, 10m architecture/tradeoffs, 20m demo, 10m live Q&A. Keep CTAs simple: trial credits, bench kit, sales intro.
sanya: Messaging pillars we should lock into battlecard: 'Unified runtime', 'Cost-aware controls', 'Predictable SLOs', 'Graceful degradation & fallbacks'. Need 1-line cues for each for quick SDR use.
derek: Draft 1-liners (feel free to shorten):
```
Unified runtime — One API, same ops & dev experience across hosted, dedicated, and private.
Cost-aware controls — Batching, caching, and quantization suggestions to lower unit economics without quality surprises.
Predictable SLOs — SLA-backed throughput and latency tiers with routing policies.
Graceful degradation — Automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants/regions to stay online.
```
sam-bot: Reminder: update the battlecard doc and tag #sales-playbook when ready. Deadline request: Fri EOD.
maria: Owners: aj -> bench scripts; leo -> slides + demo; sanya -> battlecard draft; derek -> SDR routing flow. Sync tomorrow 9:00am. :thumbsup:
aj: I'll start a bench checklist and paste results to the doc by Wed.
leo: I'll prototype demo flows and a short recording for the webinar landing page.
sanya: I'll draft the battlecard and include competitor mapping + objection handlers.
derek: I'll draft the SDR flowchart and a 2-slide cheat sheet for demos.
maria: Great — thanks team. Keep updates in the doc and drop quick blockers here.
